## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceDao — core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/RaceDao.kt

## Trigger

RaceRepositoryImpl.replaceReference calling into the DAO — observed

## Today

RaceRepositoryImpl.replaceReference calls raceDao.clearReferenceFlag()
as one statement, then, when a new race is given, calls persist(race)
which runs raceDao.upsert(...) as a second, separately-transacted
statement. Each of clearReferenceFlag and upsert runs in its own Room
transaction (upsert already carries its own @Transaction), so a reader
of observeReference or observeAll can read the database between the
two: a moment where every row has isReference = false and no reference
exists, even though the caller asked to replace one reference with
another, never to remove it.

## Expected

Clearing the reference flag and writing the new reference race happen
in one Room transaction, so no read ever observes a state with no
reference during a replacement. RaceDao gains a single @Transaction
default method — following the pattern already used by RaceDao.upsert
and RaceDao.delete — that calls clearReferenceFlag() and then the
insert/upsert of the new reference race and its children, and
RaceRepositoryImpl.replaceReference calls that one method instead of
the two separate DAO calls it makes today. When race is null, the
transaction still runs, clearing the flag with no compensating write,
which is not a gap — one row changing under one transaction is already
atomic.
